transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-23
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (AE), Carlos Mendes (SE) - Redwood; Ravi Shah (CTO), Maya Lopez (ML Eng), Jordan Price (Cloud Eng) - NexaHealth

Summary: quick onboarding check-in; environment access remains the main blocker (VPC/service account/egress). Plan to run benchmark next week once access is confirmed. Discussed dedicated vs hosted for latency/cost tradeoffs and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS).

00:00 Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, quick agenda is 1) access + env readiness 2) pilot benchmark status 3) tuning notes (batching/quantization) 4) next steps. Ravi, anything to add?
00:22 Ravi Shah: no, that covers it. main thing is we need the POC to prove latency at 150ms p50 for our typical 512 token chat flows, otherwise the UX team will push back.
00:38 Carlos Mendes: okay, that latency target helps. Just to confirm, that 150ms is end-to-end excluding network to our client right? or is it server-side only?
:45 Ravi Shah: server-side, from Redwood API to response complete.
00:52 Carlos Mendes: got it, good. Maya, how's the dataset preprocessing? are you able to produce the 1k sample prompts we asked for?
01:06 Maya Lopez: yes we're about 70% through, had to clean system prompts; should finish by tomorrow. some prompts include long contexts up to 2k tokens so we'll sample down to 512 for the standard bench.
01:25 Lena Park: perfect. Jordan, can you give a quick update on VPC/service account and firewall? last week you mentioned waiting on stacking change.
01:36 Jordan Price: yeah, so we created the dev-VPC peering but the security team is blocking outbound egress to the internet for the subnet we wanted. we can either open specific IP ranges or route via a NAT gateway. also we need to add the Redwood service account that Carlos shared yesterday.
01:55 Carlos Mendes: thanks — we sent a sample IP range and the service account email. the minimal egress is to allow our control plane + model pull endpoints; for Dedicated you won't need internet outbound from the compute plane if you run air-gapped, but for this pilot the quickest path is to allow the small set of ip ranges.
02:20 Jordan Price: understood. Security asking for SOC 2 and the network diagram before they sign off.
02:30 Lena Park: absolutely — I'll attach SOC 2 and a redwood network diagram after the call. Carlos, can you also include the firewall excerpt and the exact port list?
02:38 Carlos Mendes: will do.
03:05 Ravi Shah: on data residency, we need logs to be retained for 90 days and a way to disable optional telemetry. is that possible?
03:16 Carlos Mendes: yes — for Dedicated we can configure retention and disable analytics; for hosted there's controls too, but Dedicated gives you full control.
03:26 Maya Lopez: quick question on KMS — we use HashiCorp Vault for keys, can Redwood integrate?
03:33 Carlos Mendes: we support KMS integrations, including customer-managed CMKs and HSMs in the Dedicated/private model. integration patterns vary; for pilot we can demo using a temporary managed key, and later swap to Vault via our connector.
03:48 Maya Lopez: ok that works for now.
04:05 Ravi Shah: what about SSO? we want SAML so engineers can log in through our Okta.
04:10 Lena Park: we support SAML SSO and will need your metadata. we'll send the SSO guide.
04:18 Jordan Price: thanks, we'll prioritize.

05:00 Carlos Mendes: shifting to benchmark plan — plan is to run two experiments: 1) latency baseline on hosted small model variants, 2) throughput run on Dedicated-equivalent with batching to measure p50/p95. We suggested starting with 512-token samples.
05:20 Maya Lopez: question — how does Redwood's KV cache affect our numbers? some prompts have repeated prefixes, will that skew latency?
05:31 Carlos Mendes: good point. KV cache speeds up repeated prefixes, so if your workload reuses context we expect lower average token cost and latency. for the benchmark we'll run both cold (no cache) and warm cache runs. there may be some transcription here, I said 'K V cache' earlier so apologies if that shows up weird.
06:00 Ravi Shah: and quantization? you mentioned quantization profiles could impact quality. we need to ensure answer quality stays above our threshold.
06:14 Carlos Mendes: yep, Redwood Optimize recommends quantization presets per model and workload. for the pilot we can keep full precision for the quality pass and try 4-bit for cost pass, compare outputs using your eval set.
06:30 Maya Lopez: sounds good. what's the timing for the benchmark?
06:34 Carlos Mendes: once Jordan confirms service account + egress (target 7/24), we can run bench 7/29 and deliver results 7/30.
06:42 Jordan Price: 7/24 for access seems doable if security has the doc.

10:15 Lena Park: some questions from internal: are there concerns about canary rollouts for model changes in production? we support canary percentages and auto fallback if latency spikes.
10:30 Ravi Shah: yes, we'd like automatic fallback and observability per route. also want per-token cost visibility per customer.
10:40 Carlos Mendes: those are both standard — Console provides token-level cost and latencies per route and we can configure auto-fallback policies.

12:00 Maya Lopez: for the integration, do you have SDKs in python and node? we prefer python.
12:06 Lena Park: yes we have SDKs and quickstart samples; I'll include the python snippet in follow-up.

15:20 Jordan Price: small nit — our security asked about 3rd party comps; we run periodic pen tests. who handles incident response?
15:30 Carlos Mendes: Redwood has incident response playbooks and for enterprise customers we provide runbooks and postmortems; for Dedicated/Private we can align on contact lists.

18:05 Ravi Shah: ok let's surface blockers: 1) security sign-off pending SOC2 + network diagram 2) egress/service account 3) finalize 1k sample prompts 4) confirm benchmark date. anything else?
18:25 Lena Park: that matches our list. I'll recap action items at the end.

25:00 Maya Lopez: one more technical — how do you handle autoscaling for burst traffic? we saw mention of burst capacity in docs.
25:12 Carlos Mendes: Dedicated supports burst capacity off a reserved pool; policy is configurable and can be set to auto-scale keeping latency SLO. for hosted we have tiered capacity.
25:40 Ravi Shah: cost question — what's the rough delta between hosted and Dedicated for our expected profile?
25:50 Lena Park: rough rule: hosted is simpler but can be more expensive per token at scale. Dedicated with reserved capacity and batching typically reduces unit cost 30-50% depending on utilization and quantization. we'll send a pricing worksheet with sample math.
26:20 Jordan Price: please include an example for 2M tokens/month and 20% warm cache.

35:00 Carlos Mendes: quick note on telemetry — we can disable optional telemetry and restrict logs; audit logs are available for Dedicated in your cloud or through our control plane exports.
35:18 Ravi Shah: great.

41:00 Lena Park: recap and next steps: 1) Lena sends SOC2 + network diagram + python quickstart + Dedicated pricing worksheet 2) Carlos sends firewall ip list + SSO guide + runs bench when access is ready 3) Jordan to confirm service account + egress by 7/24 4) Maya to finalize sample prompts by 7/24 5) Benchmark run targeted 7/29 with results 7/30.
41:45 Ravi Shah: that works. one ask — can you also include a short doc on quantization/regression testing methodology?
41:55 Carlos Mendes: yes I'll add a brief note and an eval harness template.
42:05 Lena Park: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and I'll create the calendar invite for the benchmark run.
42:20 Jordan Price: thanks, bye.
42:25 All: bye.

Meeting end.
